Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral widening of the paraspinal lines (lateral displacement), which is a classic radiographic sign of a posterior mediastinal mass. In the context of the provided options, this finding is most consistent with lymphoma (e.g., Hodgkin lymphoma involving paravertebral nodes), and such masses can sometimes be asymptomatic regarding respiration until they reach a significant size or invade adjacent structures.
